description: How a Databricks metric view is read. Its YAML definition lists the dimensions (`fields` and `dimensions`) and measures the model is offered, the tables it reads (`source` and the `joins` beneath it), its typed `parameters`, and the prose that becomes first-touch and retrieval context. A member written without a name is a wildcard, expanded from the view's column metadata. Both packages read the same definition into the same model.

specifications.description: A view's id, its YAML definition, the column metadata `DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED ... AS JSON` reports when the case has `columns`, and the model read from them. `description` is the catalog comment, used when the YAML has no `comment`. A dependency is a three-part name, parsed as `qualified_names` pins; a source that is not one, such as a query, leaves the dependencies incomplete. The view's `filter` is SQL it always applies, so it is described in the context and is not a member. `expected` is the model, `unsupported` with the names the reason must mention, or an error.

cases.name: joins, a filter, and prose become dependencies and context
cases.yaml:
version: 1.1
comment: Governed order metrics.
ai_context: Treat returned orders as active.
source: main.sales.orders
filter: source.is_active
joins:
  - name: customer
    source: main.sales.customers
    on: source.customer_id = customer.id
    cardinality: many_to_one
    joins:
      - name: region
        source: "`main`.`sales`.`sales regions`"
        using: [region_id]
fields:
  - name: region
    expr: region.name
    display_name: Region
    comment: Sales region.
    synonyms: [territory]
measures:
  - name: revenue
    expr: SUM(source.revenue)
    comment: Booked revenue.

expected.name: order_metrics
first_touch: Metric-view relationship `customer` joins `main.sales.customers` on source.customer_id = customer.id with many_to_one cardinality.
Metric-view relationship `region` joins ``main`.`sales`.`sales regions`` on using region_id.
retrieval: Metric-view relationship `customer` joins `main.sales.customers` on source.customer_id = customer.id with many_to_one cardinality.
Metric-view relationship `region` joins ``main`.`sales`.`sales regions`` on using region_id.

mentions: wildcard members require concrete column metadata

qualified_names.description: A dotted name split into its parts. A backtick-quoted part keeps dots and spaces, and a doubled backtick inside one is a backtick. Unquoted whitespace or an unclosed quote makes it no name at all, which is an empty list.

type_text.description: A column's type, as metadata reports it, written as the member's type. A string is kept. A structured type is written by name, with its precision and scale or its length where the type has them. Anything else has no type.

relation_kinds.description: Which listed relations are metric views, from `information_schema.tables.table_type` and the object type the warehouse's table metadata reports. Either type mentioning `metric` makes a metric view, then either mentioning `view` makes a view, and anything else is a table. Unity Catalog's table metadata reports a metric view as `VIEW`.

selection.description: Which metric views a `tables` selection reads up front, which it leaves as stubs, and which relations remain tables. The listing reports metric views among the relations, as `relation_kinds` pins. A metric view an entry names exactly is read up front, and one that cannot be used fails the selection. A namespace's metric views are stubs. A metric view over exactly named tables is read up front when those tables include every table it reads, and is skipped quietly when it cannot be read or used. `exclude` drops metric views by name. `warehouse` is the catalog every case reads, all in main.sales, which is the connection's current namespace.

metric_views.order_metrics:
version: 1.1
source: main.sales.orders
dimensions:
  - name: region
    expr: region
measures:
  - name: revenue
    expr: SUM(total)
metric_views.joined_metrics:
version: 1.1
source: main.sales.orders
joins:
  - name: customer
    source: main.sales.customers
    on: source.customer_id = customer.id
measures:
  - name: customers
    expr: COUNT(DISTINCT customer.id)
metric_views.wildcard_metrics:
version: 1.1
source: main.sales.orders
dimensions:
  - expr: "*"
measures:
  - name: orders
    expr: COUNT(1)
metric_views.tagged_metrics:
version: 1.1
source: main.sales.orders
parameters:
  - name: tags
    data_type: ARRAY<STRING>
measures:
  - name: orders
    expr: COUNT(1)

cases.name: a namespace's metric views are stubs
an exact metric view is read
metric views over an exact table are brought in when it covers every table they read
a joined metric view needs every table it reads selected
exclude drops listed metric views
an exact metric view with an unsupported parameter fails the selection
an exact metric view with wildcards and no column metadata fails the selection

metric_sql.description: The query a call over a metric view's measures compiles to. Measures are read with `MEASURE()` under their own names, dimensions are selected and grouped by, each `where` entry compares a dimension as `semantic-models.json` and the Snowflake fixture describe, and each `arguments` name is passed to the view as a `?` bind. Identifiers are written as Databricks quotes them, in backticks; R renders with `DBI::ANSI()` and its runner swaps the double quotes for backticks. A string literal escapes a quote or a backslash with a backslash, because Databricks reads a doubled quote as two adjacent literals.

cases.name: measures alone
dimensions are selected and grouped by

expected.sql: SELECT `region`, `tier`, MEASURE(`revenue`) AS `revenue`, MEASURE(`orders`) AS `orders` FROM `main`.`sales`.`order_metrics` GROUP BY `region`, `tier`

cases.name: a where value is quoted or written bare

expected.sql: SELECT `region`, MEASURE(`revenue`) AS `revenue` FROM `main`.`sales`.`order_metrics` WHERE (`region` = 'O\'Brien') AND (`tier` > 2) GROUP BY `region`

cases.name: a backslash in a where value is escaped, so it cannot end the literal
parameters are passed to the view
a where column must be a dimension
